interpret.subject: deposit_address
interpret.derivation: Fresh service-controlled address per order (P2SH in both samples), printed on the order page with a QR code and in the letter; the service assigns no order number ('We do not attribute ID tracking numbers to your orders') and the FAQ tells the user to monitor this address on a block explorer

interpret.subject: order_id
interpret.text: The service assigns no order identifier ('We do not attribute ID tracking numbers to your orders'); the deposit address is the only per-order value.

interpret.subject: deposit_txid
interpret.text: Tier-1 fact; the service shows no status, so even a funded order would expose it only on-chain. best_persistence is provisional.

interpret.subject: amounts
interpret.text: At tier 0 this is the payment amount requested in the amount mode (forward_amount) and the deposit window the order page computes from it; deposit and payout amounts are tier-1. In this case the requested amount reached no disk source.

interpret.subject: fee_and_delay
interpret.text: The user chooses neither fee nor delay; the service sets both at random within published bounds, and the letter prints only the bounds (service constants).

interpret.subject: session_id
interpret.text: The service keeps no session: the order is created and shown in one POST response and never referenced again.

interpret.subject: client_ip
interpret.text: Unlike a DDoS-Guard front, Cloudflare exposes nothing of the client's address to the browser; a search needs the IP from another source (notes.yaml could record the VM's public address).

interpret.subject: user_identifier
interpret.text: Account-less and code-less: 'There is no need in using mixer-codes' (home page).

interpret.subject: status_progression
interpret.text: The service shows no order status at any stage (status.mechanism none).

We neither require registration nor store logs. Once the mixing is done and transaction confirmed, the data on processed transactions is deleted. Following up to 7 days during which we expect to receive your deposit, the data also gets erased.

About 16 hours after the capture every replayed request, including those carrying the recorded cf_clearance cookie, was answered by Cloudflare's challenge page; the service was not reached, so whether it still held the orders is unknown

No request reached the origin on replay, and the service offers no lookup that could show whether an order record exists; the 7-day validity can only be tested by a deposit or by re-submitting a destination address and comparing deposit addresses, which was not done.

beyond_disk.subject: Letter of Guarantee
beyond_disk.scheme_notes: Signature packet: version 4, type 0x01 (canonical text), RSA, SHA1, issuer key id D3B280956F0E7CAF, which is the tail of the fingerprint the site publishes (B8A5 CFCA F63F F2D8 384A 6B12 D3B2 8095 6F0E 7CAF) and links to /pgp-key.txt; the fingerprint printed inside the letter is a different key. The signature's own creation time equals the capture clock (UTC) while the printed 'GMT' time is two hours later: the server prints local time labelled GMT. The FAQ tells users to verify with Gpg4win or the 'PGP Checker' at bitlist.co.
beyond_disk.verification_notes: Investigator task: the signature should be verified against the published key (/pgp-key.txt) and the identity it names.
